messages:
Maria (security): Heads-up: need a final plan for cross-region TLS hardening across eu-west and ap-southeast services. Scope: mTLS rollout, cert lifecycle (rotation & revocation), KMS/HSM integration for private keys, and audit log fields for compliance. Asking eng/sre + infra for tradeoffs.
Liam (sre): +1. Are we doing per-region CAs or one global CA with region-signed leaf certs?
Dmitri (infra): Prefer local intermediate CAs per region signed by global root (so private key gravity stays region-small). Means we can revoke/regenerate region intermediate without global outages.
Anna (ops): Ops question: how do we store the root/intermediate keys? HSM or KMS? We need to meet customer reqs for key custody (HSM-backed) for some enterprise deals.
Maria (security): Exactly. For enterprise accounts we must support customer-managed keys (BYOK) in KMS + HSM option. For platform-owned keys, default to KMS with HSM-protected keys (AWS KMS with key material in CloudHSM / GCP External HSM).
DevSecBot: Automated check: current cipher suites include TLS1.2 fallback. Recommendation: TLS1.3-only for service-to-service where supported. Flagging services w/ legacy clients: billing-api, metrics-forwarder.
Liam (sre): Implementation notes: use mTLS with short-lived certs (1h-24h depending on workload) issued by regional intermediate CA. Use Vault PKI or cert-manager (in-cluster) to auto-sign. Use KMS/Vault transit to encrypt private keys at rest.
Dmitri (infra): For HSM-backed root we propose: global root private key in HSM (offline), intermediate keys generated in region HSM where available. If KMS only in some regions, wrap intermediate keys with KMS CMKs and store wrapped blobs in Vault.
Maria (security): Audit log requirements: every TLS handshake must emit cert fingerprint, issuer, subject, service identity (service-name), principal identity (svc account), and validation result. Send to SIEM with immutable retention and signed log chain.
Sophie (privacy): Also include purpose/consent tag for customer-provided keys and record KMS key alias used per cert issuance for auditability.
Anna (ops): Quick config snippet for Envoy TLS to enforce mTLS and TLS1.3:
```yaml
common_tls_context:
  tls_certificates:
  - certificate_chain: { filename: "/etc/certs/tls.crt" }
    private_key: { filename: "/etc/certs/tls.key" }
  alpn_protocols: [h2, http/1.1]
  tls_params:
    tls_minimum_protocol_version: TLSv1_3
    cipher_suites: [] # TLS1.3 uses default suites
validation_context:
  trusted_ca: { filename: "/etc/certs/ca.pem" }
  match_subject_alt_names:
  - exact: "spiffe://redwood.local/service/my-service"
```
Liam (sre): Notes on cert rotation: cert-manager can request intermediate-signed certs and write into k8s secrets, but we must ensure secret encryption at rest (KMS). For non-k8s workloads, agents fetch from Vault via mTLS and store in ephemeral tmpfs.
Dmitri (infra): Example OpenSSL command to fingerprint certs for audits:
```bash
openssl x509 -in tls.crt -noout -fingerprint -sha256 | sed 's/^.*=//'
```
Maria (security): KMS integration Qs: 1) Do we wrap private keys with KMS CMKs or use KMS-backed signing (asymmetric keys)? 2) How do we rotate KMS keys without breaking certs?
Dmitri (infra): Options: - Use KMS asymmetric keys for signing CSR -> pros: private key never leaves KMS. cons: limited algorithms/ops and latency. - Use KMS to wrap intermediate private key blobs stored in Vault -> pros: flexible, still HSM-backed wrapping, easier rotation. For rotation: create new CMK, rewrap existing blobs, update intermediate cert key references, and roll intermediate certs if needed.
Liam (sre): For zero-downtime: issue new intermediate signed by root, provision in parallel, roll trust stores, then retire old intermediate after TTL. Avoid reissuing all leaf certs at once.
Anna (ops): RBAC changes: we'll need new service roles: cert-issuer (can request/synthesize certs), cert-rotator (can rotate secrets), cert-auditor (read-only view of issuance logs). Map to team service accounts and restrict to namespaces/regions.
Maria (security): Also require MFA + approval for root-level operations (create/rotate root key, sign intermediate). Documented runbook for emergency revocation.
Sophie (privacy): Add retention policy for certificate logs (7 years for compliance) and mask PII fields in logs where possible.
DevSecBot: Vulnerability scan: Dependabot flagged OpenSSL 1.1 libs on metrics-forwarder image. That blocks TLS1.3 only plan for that service. Ticket created: #INV-482.
Liam (sre): Action items: 1) Dmitri -> draft HSM/KMS design doc and rewrap strategy (due Tue). 2) Anna -> list services that can't speak TLS1.3 (due EOD). 3) Maria -> audit log schema + SIEM ingestion spec (due Wed). 4) SRE team -> plan rollout waves per region (prep by next week).
Dmitri (infra): I'll include example KMS key alias patterns: kms:alias/redwood/root, kms:alias/redwood/region-eu/intermediate. Also include CMK tags: {env, region, purpose}.
Maria (security): Thanks. If we agree on the approach, we'll schedule a short design review Wed 09:30 UTC. Please add notes to the design doc: /docs/security/tls-cross-region (WIP).
Anna (ops): ack. I'll start inventorying services and talk to app owners. :thumbsup: 
Liam (sre): ack. I'll follow up on the metrics-forwarder upgrade and prepare Envoy/sidecar rollout plan.
DevSecBot: Reminder: run whitelist scan after changes and add policy tests for tls_minimum_protocol_version >= TLSv1_3.
Maria (security): Great thread. We'll capture final decisions in the design doc and make tickets for RBAC changes and audit log pipelines.
